correctness.rationale: For every q>=3 and n>=3 the exact legal-swap criterion forces prefix aba. Local inspection of all intervening a-free blocks gives a unique finite block grammar with three complete-block kinds and three terminal-tail kinds. Multiplying their weights gives the full multivariate enumerator. The univariate denominator factors algebraically and yields a weighted-tribonacci recurrence. The maximal length with k initial-symbol occurrences is 4k-3, attained by aba(cbca)^(k-2)cb; this excludes balanced q>=4 and small ternary multiplicities. An explicit balanced ternary family exists for all m>=3 and coefficient extraction yields exactly 6*binomial(2m-3,m). The standalone exact checker compared direct star swaps and grammar composition histograms for 26 alphabet/length cases, confirmed recurrence, six balanced coefficients and 22 constructive multiplicities. Proof does not depend on the finite check.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither unrestricted star-swap connectivity nor constrained adjacent-swap reachability subsumes the intersection of properness and first-position-to-arbitrary-position swaps. A statement about fewer or different edges cannot bound the new degree-zero counts without an explicit reduction, and examples show the two zero-degree predicates are incomparable.

originality.rationale: The closest star-swap monograph/paper considers unrestricted multiset permutations; a nonlocal first-position exchange with an additional adjacent-inequality constraint changes the graph and creates frozen states. The closest proper-coloring reconfiguration paper permits exchanges only along an edge of the original path, i.e. adjacent-position swaps. The present star-frozen composition series and ternary/four-symbol equal-content threshold are not consequences of either. The accessed published index and accessible historical result summaries yielded no equivalent count. Residual literature-priority risk is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: A previous equivalent enumeration of proper-word first-position star-swap isolated vertices under unsearched terminology cannot be excluded.
Results about unrestricted star-transposition graph connectivity cannot be used to infer connectedness after the proper-word restriction.
No conclusion about Hamiltonicity for q>=4 equal-composition classes follows solely from the absence of frozen states.

value.rationale: The question is naturally motivated by generating fixed-composition strings through local legal changes while preserving an adjacent-inequality (homopolymer-free) constraint. A frozen word is an absolute obstruction to a spanning star-transposition Gray code, and exact counts by every content vector quantify that obstruction. The sharp alphabet transition at equal multiplicities and the closed binomial ternary census go beyond a mere finite example; the weighted-tribonacci total law and max-length frequency barrier cover all lengths and alphabets. This does not purport to characterize all nontrivial components or solve the unrestricted Gray-code problem.
